name: Fat Gripz / grip thickeners

lead: Fat Gripz wrap around a bar to make it thicker so the hands and forearms work harder when holding it. They are marketed for forearm thickening.
Only one acute study on strength and muscle activation was found; forearm growth has not been tested in the sources reviewed.

paras: A thicker handle reduces how well the fingers can wrap around it, increasing the demand on the grip muscles.
No adverse effects were documented in the sources reviewed.

studies.title: Impact of Fat Grip Attachments on Muscular Strength and Neuromuscular Activation During Resistance Exercise.
studies.source: Journal of strength and conditioning research

lead: Fat Gripz are thick rubber sleeves that attach to a barbell, dumbbell or handle to increase its diameter, making it harder to hold. They are used in strength training with the aim of challenging grip and forearm muscles.

One study examined the acute effects of Fat Gripz on muscle activation and strength in 15 resistance-trained men [1]. The sources available here give no data on long-term forearm size changes, so this article is brief.

paras: A 2021 study in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research examined the acute effects of Fat Gripz on muscular activation and strength during resistance exercise in 15 resistance-trained men, who performed two experimental conditions [1]. Details of the results were not available in the abstract text reviewed. No longer-term trials on forearm thickness were found.
Grip strength is the force the hand applies to hold or pull an object, and thick-bar holds are among the methods listed for training the closing grip [2].
